title: Too Many Voices at the Fire

collection.credit:
NEW EVENTS — ADVICE AND DECISIONS (ADV-01..50, draft for the owner, 2026-11-15)
Asking for advice, giving it, ignoring it, following half of it, and deciding alone. Advice can be wrong, even from elders and experts. Following it doesn't guarantee a good outcome and ignoring it doesn't cause a bad one. Feeling heard with no decision is a perfectly good ending, and nobody ever has to admit someone else was right.
Written in the style of the owner's own events. Edit anything and send it back; nothing ships until you approve.

ledger.why: the casting line, carried out as the roles' ages (picks an adult)

collection.description: A villager mentions goats in the garden and everyone at the fire has advice: thank everyone and leave, or pick the funniest idea.

setup.name: The setup
setup.text: (name1) mentions at the fire that (his/her) neighbor's goats keep eating (his/her) garden. Immediately everyone has a solution. Build a fence. Talk to the neighbor. Plant something goats hate. Get a dog. Get a bigger goat. Move. Within a minute (name1) is surrounded by advice, and none of it is the same.

o1.name: Outcome A
o1.text: "Thank you all," says (name1), standing up. "I'm going to go and think." (He/she) walks along the beach alone until the voices fade. Then (he/she) sits on a rock and thinks about what (he/she) actually wants: to keep (his/her) beans and stay friends with the neighbor. The next morning (he/she) goes and talks to the neighbor. Nobody at the fire suggested exactly that, though several of them later remember that they did.

o2.name: Outcome B
o2.text: "Who said get a bigger goat?" asks (name1). Somebody raises a hand. "Why?" "A bigger goat would scare the little goats away." Everyone stops to consider this. It is, strangely, not the worst idea. It's not a good one either. The whole fire spends the evening arguing about goats, and (name1) sits back and enjoys it. The beans are still a problem tomorrow.
